_comment: Backs the Constitution's 'layered-complexity' law (scripts/policy/constitution.json) -- the 'basic features stay simple by default' half, which ledger/boundaries/B32.yml originally called impossible to check ('no failing input that proves a feature IS too complex, only a design review judgment'). This does not attempt to judge complexity directly. It operationalizes the law as a RATCHET, the same shape scripts/policy/coverage-baseline.json already uses for test coverage: the mandatory (JSON Schema `required`) surface of the platform's basic building blocks -- the fields a first-time author cannot avoid declaring -- must never grow silently. A silent grow means some change made a basic feature harder to start with by default; check-layered-complexity-ratchet.py fails the moment `requiredCount` for any watched definition exceeds the value recorded here. Raising a count on purpose (a real new mandatory field with a real reason) means bumping this file in the SAME commit, with the reason in `note` -- exactly coverage-baseline.json's own discipline.
note: Initial baseline, this session: measured directly from NPDevContract/schemas/model.schema.json, not assumed. Every watched definition already sits at 2 required keys -- name plus exactly one other structural key (fields/type/route/steps) -- which is why the floor starts here rather than at some invented target.
